mainTopic: מתוך שהותרה לצורך הותרה נמי שלא לצורך: carrying non-food items on יום טוב, the עולת נדבה ברייתא, רבה's alternative and רב יוסף's rebuttal, and רבי יוחנן's proof from גיד הנשה
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the previous sugya, which explains the ציר (hinge) dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל as a question of whether we make a גזירה. Then a new משנה begins: בית שמאי forbid carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the public domain on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it. The גמרא brings a ברייתא that one who slaughters an עולת נדבה on יום טוב gets מלקות. רבי יצחק בר אבדימי says this follows only בית שמאי. בית הלל hold the principle of מתוך: once a מלאכה is permitted for a food need, it is permitted even without one, and that would apply to slaughter too. רבה suggests the משנה's dispute is instead about whether הוצאה applies on יום טוב at all. רב יוסף rejects this, because then the משנה should have argued about carrying stones, so the dispute must be about הוצאה שלא לצורך. The גמרא adds that רבי יוחנן also holds this. It begins to prove it from a ברייתא about cooking גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב, which earns five sets of מלקות. The fifth is completed on the next amud.

steps.title: The hinge dispute is about whether to make a protective decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up the previous discussion. בית שמאי make a גזירה forbidding a middle hinge because people might confuse it with a side hinge. בית הלל do not make that גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that we decree against a hinge in the middle because of a hinge on the side, and the other Sage holds that we do not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of the previous sugya. It explains what the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל about hinges really comes down to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that fixing a hinge in the middle is not itself real building. The only argument is whether we forbid it anyway, as a fence (גזירה), because it looks like fixing a side hinge, which would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage holds; used to lay out the two sides of a dispute
We make a rabbinic decree (גזירה) as a protective fence
A hinge or pivot of a door or lid
Because of; out of concern for confusion with

steps.whatToRemember: The hinge dispute is not about the basic law. It is only about whether to add a protective גזירה.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: we decree

phrases.aramaic: צִיר בָּאֶמְצַע אַטּוּ צִיר מִן הַצַּד,
phrases.english: against a hinge in the middle because of a hinge on the side,
and the other Sage holds: we do not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: גָּזְרִינַן צִיר בָּאֶמְצַע אַטּוּ צִיר מִן הַצַּד, וּמָר סָבַר: לָא גָּזְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the hinge discussion from the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement over a middle hinge comes down to whether we make a גזירה because of a side hinge.

steps.title: Carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. בית שמאי forbid carrying a small child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the public domain on יום טוב. בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: one may not carry out a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the public domain on יום טוב. בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It records an argument about carrying things on יום טוב that have nothing to do with food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, carrying (הוצאה) is clearly allowed for food needs. A child, a לולב, and a ספר תורה are not food needs. So the question is whether carrying is allowed only for food, or for other needs too.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
Carry out from a private domain to a public one
The public domain
The palm branch taken on סוכות
They permit

steps.confusionAlert: This is יום טוב, not שבת. On שבת everyone agrees carrying into the public domain is forbidden. The argument here exists only because יום טוב already allows carrying for food.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:
one may not carry out neither a minor child,
nor the lulav,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: nor a Torah scroll into the public domain,
phrases.notes: None of these are needed for food.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the hinge discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid carrying non-food items like a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the public domain on יום טוב. בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: A ברייתא: slaughtering an עולת נדבה on יום טוב earns מלקות
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רבי יצחק בר אבדימי. It says that one who slaughters an עולת נדבה on יום טוב receives מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רבי יצחק בר אבדימי: One who slaughters an עולת נדבה on יום טוב receives מלקות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say slaughtering is forbidden on יום טוב when it is not for food. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely on the מזבח, so no person eats from it. An עולת נדבה is also optional, not a required offering. So slaughtering it on יום טוב serves no food need, and the ברייתא treats it as a forbidden מלאכה deserving מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (a reciter of ברייתות) taught
Before him; in his presence
A voluntary burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Receives lashes (מלקות)

steps.confusionAlert: The תנא here is not a sage of the משנה. He is a professional reciter who memorized ברייתות and recited them in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Tanna taught
before Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹחֵט עוֹלַת נְדָבָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב — לוֹקֶה.
phrases.english: One who slaughters a voluntary burnt offering on Yom Tov receives lashes.
phrases.notes: No one eats it, so this is slaughter not for food.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא connected to the משנה's question: are מלאכות allowed on יום טוב only for food?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering an עולת נדבה on יום טוב is punishable by מלקות.

steps.title: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי says the ברייתא follows only בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי tells the תנא that the ברייתא must follow בית שמאי. בית שמאי do not hold the principle that a מלאכה permitted for a need is also permitted without that need.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who said this to you? It is בית שמאי, who say: we do not say that since carrying was permitted for a need, it was also permitted not for a need.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי reacts to the ברייתא. He limits it to the opinion of בית שמאי, which means it is not the accepted halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links the ברייתא to our משנה. בית שמאי forbid carrying a child because they hold carrying is allowed only for food. The same logic would make slaughtering a non-food offering forbidden, so the ברייתא matches בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Whose opinion is this?
Since it was permitted; the name of the principle of מתוך
Carrying from one domain to another
For a need; here, a food need

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the principle of מתוך enters the sugya. Since halacha follows בית הלל, the principle has wide practical effect on יום טוב.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who is it that said this to you?
It is Beit Shammai, who say:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּתְּרָה הוֹצָאָה לְצוֹרֶךְ —
phrases.english: we do not say: since carrying was permitted for a need,
it was also permitted not for a need.
phrases.notes: This is why בית שמאי forbid carrying a child in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ מַנִּי — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ברייתא by limiting it to בית שמאי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ברייתא is not rejected outright. It is limited to בית שמאי's view, so it is not the accepted halacha.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא assumes a מלאכה is allowed on יום טוב only for a food need, which is בית שמאי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא that one who slaughters an עולת נדבה on יום טוב gets מלקות follows בית שמאי, who reject the principle of מתוך.

steps.title: Why it cannot be בית הלל: the principle of מתוך applies to slaughter too
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא followed בית הלל, they would apply מתוך to slaughter as well. Slaughter is permitted for food, so it would also be permitted without a food need, and there would be no מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it were בית הלל, they say: since carrying was permitted for a need, it was also permitted not for a need. Here too, since slaughter was permitted for a need, it was also permitted not for a need.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי proves his point. He shows that בית הלל's logic in the משנה would also allow slaughtering the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל permit carrying a child on יום טוב because carrying is already allowed for food. רבי יצחק בר אבדימי takes the same rule (מתוך) and applies it to a different מלאכה, slaughtering. Since slaughtering is allowed for food, בית הלל would allow it even for an offering no one eats, so they could not say one gets מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: For if; introduces the alternative being ruled out
Here too; applies the same logic to a new case
Ritual slaughter
Not for a need; without a food purpose

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל hold מתוך: a מלאכה permitted on יום טוב for food is permitted even without a food need. This covers carrying, and according to רבי יצחק בר אבדימי, slaughter too.

phrases.english: For if it were Beit Hillel, they say:
since carrying was permitted for a need,
it was also permitted not for a need.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּתְּרָה שְׁחִיטָה לְצוֹרֶךְ —
phrases.english: Here too, since slaughter was permitted for a need,
it was also permitted not for a need.
phrases.notes: So by בית הלל's logic there would be no מלקות for the עולת נדבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in step 4 by showing why בית הלל cannot be the author.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the ברייתא about the עולת נדבה must follow בית שמאי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית הלל's permission in the משנה to carry non-food items, based on the principle of מתוך, which applies equally to slaughter.

steps.title: רבה questions what the dispute is really about
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks how we know the מחלוקת is about מתוך. He suggests it might instead be about whether עירוב and הוצאה apply on יום טוב at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: How do you know that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about this (מתוך)? Maybe they argue about something else: whether עירוב and the איסור of carrying out apply only on שבת and not on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the earlier claim that the argument in the משנה is about מתוך. He offers a different possible reason for the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי used the משנה to prove that בית שמאי reject מתוך. רבה says the משנה does not prove that. The argument could be about something else entirely: whether the איסור of הוצאה exists on יום טוב at all. If so, the earlier proof about the ברייתא of עולת נדבה falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
From where do we know?
Perhaps
עירוב: the device that allows carrying between domains
Carrying out from one domain to another

phrases.english: Rabba strongly objected to it:
From where do you know that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
argue about this (the principle of mitokh)?
Perhaps about 'eiruv and carrying out apply to Shabbat'
'and there is no eiruv or carrying out for Yom Tov'
they are arguing.
phrases.notes: רבה is offering a different reason for why they argue.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבָּה: מִמַּאי דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּהָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the משנה that רבי יצחק בר אבדימי relied on in steps 4-5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the מחלוקת in the משנה is about מתוך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה can be explained by a different issue, whether הוצאה applies on יום טוב. So it gives no proof about מתוך.

steps.title: בית שמאי's side in רבה's explanation
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה, בית שמאי hold that עירוב and הוצאה apply on יום טוב just as they do on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master (בית שמאי) holds: עירוב and הוצאה apply to שבת, and עירוב and הוצאה also apply to יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how בית שמאי would think according to רבה's new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, carrying on יום טוב is a real מלאכה. It is permitted only for food needs. So carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה, which are not food needs, is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds
For יום טוב (the Festival)

phrases.english: One master (Beit Shammai) holds:
eiruv and carrying out apply to Shabbat,
and eiruv and carrying out apply to Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of רבה's proposed מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the איסור of הוצאה applies on יום טוב as on שבת.

steps.title: בית הלל's side, based on a verse
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה, בית הלל hold there is no איסור of הוצאה on יום טוב. They learn this from a פסוק in ירמיה that mentions only שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other master (בית הלל) holds: עירוב and הוצאה apply to שבת, but there is no עירוב or הוצאה on יום טוב. As it is written: 'Do not carry a burden out of your houses on the שבת day.' On שבת, yes. On יום טוב, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית הלל's view in רבה's explanation and backs it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'on the שבת day,' which suggests the איסור of carrying is limited to שבת. So for בית הלל, carrying on יום טוב is simply allowed. This has nothing to do with מתוך. That is why רבה says the משנה proves nothing about מתוך.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
A burden or load
Yes
No

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. In רבה's version, it is בית הלל (the lenient side) who say there is no הוצאה on יום טוב at all. בית שמאי say there is.

phrases.english: And the other master (Beit Hillel) holds:
eiruv and carrying out apply to Shabbat,
but there is no eiruv or carrying out for Yom Tov,
as it is written: 'Do not carry a burden'
'out of your houses on the Shabbat day' (Jeremiah 17:22).
On Shabbat, yes (forbidden); on Yom Tov, no.
phrases.notes: We learn this because the פסוק mentions only שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of רבה's proposed מחלוקת, with its scriptural source.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's view that there is no איסור of הוצאה on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיה יז:כב, 'ולא תוציאו משא מבתיכם ביום השבת'. It mentions only שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף: then they should argue about stones
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבה. If בית הלל held there is no הוצאה on יום טוב, they would permit carrying anything, even useless stones. So the מחלוקת should have been taught about stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: But if so, let them argue about stones!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רבה's explanation by pointing to what the משנה should have said if רבה were right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית הלל held there is no איסור of carrying on יום טוב at all, they would allow carrying even things with no purpose, like stones. The משנה would then have used stones to show בית הלל's leniency most sharply. Instead, the משנה lists useful items: a child, a לולב, a ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (from now on, by your logic)
Let them argue
Stones (objects with no use on יום טוב)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objected to it:
But if so,
let them argue about stones!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's alternative explanation from steps 6-8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that בית הלל hold there is no הוצאה on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were true, בית הלל would permit carrying even useless stones. Then the מחלוקת should have been stated about stones.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins to draw his conclusion
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה does not argue about stones, רב יוסף begins to conclude something. The conclusion itself continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since they do not argue about stones, learn from this...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף is setting up his conclusion. The 'שמע מינה' here opens the next move, which finishes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that the משנה uses only items with some purpose shows that even בית הלל agree carrying on יום טוב is basically an איסור. So the real issue must be whether a need beyond food (מתוך) permits carrying. That is a return to רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Since ... not
Learn from this (a conclusion is coming)

steps.whyThisMatters: This step brings the sugya back to explaining the מחלוקת through מתוך. It supports the original reading of רבי יצחק בר אבדימי.

phrases.english: Rather, since they do not argue about stones,
learn from this,
phrases.notes: What we learn comes in the next line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִדְּלָא מִפַּלְגִי בַּאֲבָנִים, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב יוסף's challenge into a positive inference against רבה.
steps.raayaObject: That everyone agrees הוצאה is forbidden on יום טוב except for a need.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The silence of the משנה about stones. It argues only about useful items.

steps.title: The argument is about carrying that is not for a need
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finishes his conclusion: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about הוצאה שלא לצורך.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about carrying out that is not for a need.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף completes the sentence he began in the last step. Since the משנה does not argue about useless stones, he concludes that the argument must be about carrying that is not for a real need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said בית הלל hold there is no איסור הוצאה on יום טוב at all. רב יוסף showed that this can't be right, because then they would even permit carrying stones. So the argument must be narrower: carrying that is somewhat useful but not for food. בית הלל permit it because of מתוך, and בית שמאי forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying an object from a private domain to a public domain
Not for a need; here, not for food preparation on יום טוב
They argue

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's view: the מחלוקת is about הוצאה שלא לצורך, which brings us back to the principle of מתוך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings the sugya back to the original idea that the מחלוקת is about מתוך, which rejects רבה's alternative explanation.

phrases.english: They argue about carrying out that is not for a need.
phrases.notes: This completes רב יוסף's sentence earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the conclusion that רב יוסף began in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת is about carrying that is not for a need, meaning the question of מתוך.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also holds the argument is about מתוך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבי יוחנן also understands the מחלוקת to be about מתוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן also holds that they argue about the principle: since carrying was permitted for a need, it was also permitted not for a need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that רבי יוחנן agrees with רב יוסף's reading. This sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ואף ('also') shows the גמרא is lining up more support for the מתוך explanation. The principle of מתוך says: once carrying is permitted for food on יום טוב, it is permitted even without that need. The proof for רבי יוחנן's view is brought next.

keyTerms.meaning: And also; adds another authority who agrees
Since it was permitted; the principle that a מלאכה permitted for a need on יום טוב is permitted even without that need
For a need, such as food preparation

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan also holds:
about 'since carrying was permitted for a need'
it was also permitted not for a need, that they argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יוחנן as another authority who supports רב יוסף's conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן holds that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about מתוך.

steps.title: The ברייתא about cooking גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recited before רבי יוחנן that someone who cooks גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eats it gets five sets of מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a תנא taught before רבי יוחנן: one who cooks the גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eats it is flogged five times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its proof for רבי יוחנן's view by quoting a ברייתא that was recited in front of him. Here it only gives the case and the number five; the details come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case combines several איסורים in one act: גיד הנשה, בשר בחלב, and doing a מלאכה on יום טוב. The number five is the key. To reach five, the ברייתא must count מלקות for יום טוב מלאכה done without a food need, which will matter for the question of מתוך.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter who memorized and taught ברייתות in the בית מדרש
Before him; in his presence
The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating
Receives מלקות (lashes)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'five' are five separate sets of מלקות for five different איסורים, not five lashes.

phrases.english: For a reciter taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
One who cooks the sciatic nerve in milk
on a Festival and eats it
is flogged five times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that proves רבי יוחנן's view stated in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן understands the מחלוקת to be about מתוך.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recited before רבי יוחנן about cooking גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב.

steps.title: Listing the five sets of מלקות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the מלקות: cooking the גיד, eating the גיד, cooking בשר בחלב, eating בשר בחלב, and a fifth that continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is flogged for cooking the גיד, for eating the גיד, for cooking meat in milk, for eating meat in milk, and he is flogged...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains how we reach five sets of מלקות. It lists four here, and the fifth is completed on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking the גיד counts as a יום טוב violation, because the גיד is forbidden to eat, so cooking it is not food preparation. Eating the גיד is a direct Torah איסור. Cooking and eating בשר בחלב are two more separate איסורים. The fifth will show the ברייתא's view on מלאכה done on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of; on account of
Meat cooked with milk, forbidden both to cook and to eat
One who cooks

steps.confusionAlert: 'Cooking the גיד' is not the בשר בחלב איסור, since that is listed separately. It is a יום טוב violation, because cooking something that may not be eaten is not food preparation.

phrases.english: He is flogged because of cooking the nerve,
phrases.notes: It's cooking on יום טוב when it isn't for food you're allowed to eat.

phrases.english: and he is flogged because of eating the nerve,
and he is flogged because of cooking meat in milk,
and he is flogged because of eating meat in milk,
and he is flogged
phrases.notes: The fifth reason continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the five sets of מלקות announced in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each separate איסור in this single act earns its own set of מלקות. The fifth is completed on the next amud.
